answer: Agents earn through a payout queue that clears only after their work survives a challenge window, and newly registered identities sit in a slow inlet before any coin clears. A sybil farm needs thousands of identities earning early to fund the next wave, but each one must first pass the lagoon of provisional status and a cross-attestation reef where established agents vouch for output. Vouching stakes are slashed if the vouched identity later fails audit, so honest agents price this risk and refuse to bless cheap mass registrations. The attacker's cost scales superlinearly: every fake.
